facts.program: Efficiency Maine whole-home heat pump rebate
facts.claim: $1,000 (any income), $2,000 (moderate income) or $3,000 (low income) per rebate-eligible outdoor unit, up to a lifetime limit per housing unit of $3,000, $6,000 or $9,000. Heat pumps must be the primary heating system and, with any supplemental heat, sized for at least 100% of the home's peak heating load (the heat pumps alone at least 80%). Dual fuel heat pump and furnace systems are not eligible.
facts.eligibility: Low income: homeowner or a household member on MaineCare, HEAP, SNAP or TANF, verified by Efficiency Maine. Moderate income: adjusted gross income up to $70,000 (single filer) or $100,000 (joint), verified. Single-family house, two-unit duplex, condominium or mixed-use building with one or two housing units and no commercial meter; principal residence for low and moderate income; home had no natural gas utility account before the upgrade; installed by an Efficiency Maine Residential Registered Vendor; claim form emailed or postmarked within 6 months of completion. Single-zone units on Efficiency Maine's list earn a rebate; multi-zone units do not earn one but their capacity counts toward sizing.
facts.dates: No end date stated. Terms: program and incentives subject to change or termination; allow six weeks for processing.
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-10 at efficiencymaine.com/at-home/residential-heat-pump-rebates/ and /whole-home-heat-pump-rebates/. The claim form and Heat Pump Installation Requirements Checklist were not opened. Existing homes with a furnace or boiler must keep it for emergency backup only (thermostats off or at the lowest setting, power off and covered, or generator only); new construction finished on or after 1/1/2027 must have none.

facts.program: Efficiency Maine ducted whole-home heat pump rebate
facts.claim: $3,000 (any income), $6,000 (moderate income) or $9,000 (low income) per housing unit for one or more ducted heat pumps sized for at least 100% of the home's peak heating load. In an existing home all forced hot air furnaces must be removed as part of the upgrade.
facts.eligibility: Same building, income, installer and 6-month claim rules as the other whole-home systems; ducted heat pump on Efficiency Maine's list; primary heating system; principal residence for low and moderate income.

facts.program: Efficiency Maine $500 additional heat pump bonus
facts.claim: Efficiency Maine's homepage advertises a $500 additional heat pump bonus, available now through December 31, 2026. Single-wide mobile home rebates are not eligible for it.
facts.notes: Banner on efficiencymaine.com read 2026-10-10; the whole-home page footnote excludes single-wide mobile homes. Conditions and which rebates qualify were not confirmed.

facts.program: Efficiency Maine mobile home heat pump rebate
facts.claim: Single-wide mobile homes may qualify for up to $13,900 in rebates (Efficiency Maine's homepage says low-income homeowners could qualify for $13,900 by converting to a new ducted heat pump system).
facts.notes: Only the amount on the whole-home page and the homepage was read; the mobile home initiative page was not opened.

facts.claim: Fixed-rate loans for heat pumps, insulation, heat pump water heaters and batteries: 1-year 0% APR (with a $500 origination fee), 5-year 5.99% APR, 10-year 7.99% APR, and an income-based 10-year 5.99% APR loan up to $7,500. Maximum $25,000 on the standard loans, and the loan cannot exceed project cost minus the expected rebate. Rates shown are as of today and subject to change.
facts.eligibility: Maine property and principal residence, owner of the property, residential property (single family, duplex, mobile home or condo unit), installed by an Efficiency Maine Residential Registered Vendor. Borrowing capacity depends on credit (debt-to-income at most 55% and average FICO at least 620 for the full amount). Heat pump and fossil fuel dual fuel systems are not eligible.
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-10; table truncated after the borrowing limits.
